bullets.title: Rare defensive-vs-cyclical rotation signals stress beneath calm indexes
bullets.body: Citi flags defensive stocks outperforming cyclicals by up to 15 percentage points in both the U.S. and Europe — a rotation magnitude seen only in 2008, 2020, and 2022. Credit spreads have widened, earnings revisions have slowed, and AI sentiment/valuations have reset sharply lower, even as headline equity indexes look calm. U.S. Treasuries have regained flight-to-quality status, rallying when tech weakens.

bullets.title: BKX down 4 straight days, testing key support — bearish broad-market signal
bullets.body: The banking index has shed ~4.75% over three days and is trading below its 50-, 100-, and 200-day moving averages, with both daily/weekly MACD momentum negative. The analyst notes the market has failed five consecutive 'clearing events' (hedge fund de-grossing, mid-terms, NVDA CEO resignation, NVDA earnings, ANT IPO) and warns that BKX weakness historically signals the broad market cannot sustain strength, with 150 as next support (~10% lower).

bullets.title: Fed hawkish pivot: JPM forecasts three hikes (Dec/Jan/Mar) to 4.5–4.75%; rare cross-asset warning signal
bullets.body: JPMorgan's Mike Feroli projects three consecutive Fed hikes taking the funds rate to 4.5–4.75%, with core PCE falling only to 2.7% by YE28. A rare cross-asset signal has fired — S&P, Russell, and NDX all below their 200-day MAs while the 10-year yield trades above its 200-day MA, a configuration that has persisted only six times since 2008. Implied real yields have gapped higher; 10-year yield sits at ~5.08–5.097%.

bullets.title: Pre-market tape: semis and cyber lead; retailers lag on earnings
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures opened +1.02% led by semiconductor ecosystem (MU +4.6%, INTC +4.5%, STX +5.4%, WDC +5.0%) and cybersecurity (PANW +7.2%, NET +4.5%). Retailers dragged: WSM -7.6% and WMT -2.3% on earnings. VIX +3.9% to 25.51 and S&P 500 near flat on the session at ~7,299, reflecting bifurcated risk appetite.

bullets.title: US BIS China chip restrictions widen closed-model AI gap; BABA may cut 20GW data center target
bullets.body: New US BIS remote-access rules are blocking China's ability to access Nvidia chips via Southeast Asian intermediaries, favoring US closed-source AI models. TSMC and Samsung have suspended some shipments to Chinese customers pending licenses. BABA may cut its 20GW data center build target as a result; ByteDance paused a $480M chip loan and Moonshot canceled a $150M Indonesia data center deal.

bullets.title: AI capex boom faces structural headwinds: chip shortages, power bottlenecks, 30/31 data-center moratoriums
bullets.body: Consensus expects AI capital spending to rise from ~$1T in 2026 to $1.5T in 2027, but structural supply constraints are building: memory-chip executives expect 2027–2028 to be tighter with one CEO projecting a five-year shortage, power/transformer bottlenecks persist alongside chip constraints, and 30 of 31 data-center moratoriums on the ballot during election week passed. Middle East permitting timelines of 14 days vs. slower US approvals risk capacity migration offshore.

bullets.title: Manufacturing data mixed: Kansas City strong, Philly orders contracting for first time since May
bullets.body: Kansas City Fed manufacturing composite rose to 18 from 11 (ISM-equivalent 59.0 vs prior 55.5) with accelerating production, orders, and employment. Philadelphia Fed index fell 15 points to 6.3; new orders fell into contraction for the first time since May, backlogs dipped below zero, and prices paid exceeded prices received — margin pressure building. Morgan Stanley maintains November ISM Manufacturing tracking estimate at 54.7 vs. 55.5 in October.

bullets.title: Jobless claims healthy at 203k but continuing claims jump +70k to 1,763k
bullets.body: Initial claims came in at 203k vs. 198k estimate; the 4-week average is 195.75k — historically low and inconsistent with broad labor market slack. However, continuing claims jumped +70k (39k attributed to Michigan seasonal layoffs), suggesting some pockets of softening beneath the headline strength.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO priced at $83/share ($1.28T valuation); analyst sees path to $120
bullets.body: ANT priced at $83/share raising a record $81.3B, trading at ~9.8x/6.7x EV/revenue on 2027/2028 consensus estimates of $240–$250B — a 29% premium to blended hyperscaler peers and 20% premium to SPCX comps. One analyst sees upside to ~$120/share (+44%) if classified as software and valued on DDOG/PLTR multiples. Roughly 2,800 employees may hold $1M+ in options.

bullets.title: AI demand 'never been bigger' at TomorrowX; $3–5T infrastructure financing needed over next two years
bullets.body: Industry executives at TomorrowX Summit expressed no letup in AI compute demand — CRWV: 'nothing changed in 14 days'; TSMC: still doubling 2nm capacity next year. Hyperscalers hold a 2–3 year financing advantage over neoclouds via investment-grade ratings, and analysts estimate $3–5T in infrastructure financing will be required over the next two years. MSFT and ORCL seen as best positioned given cash flow scale.

bullets.title: NVDA: 103% revenue growth, $130B Q4 guide, but Jensen departure and China halt weigh on stock
bullets.body: Nvidia posted 103% annualized revenue growth with Q4 guidance of $130B and long-term growth raised to 75%, but the board publicly rejected Jensen Huang's rumored CEO return amid reported internal divisions. NVDA also halted approved Hopper data-center chip shipments to China under geopolitical pressure and faded to close -3% despite pre-market strength. QQQ drawdown stands at -11.5% from the MOAB high.

bullets.title: JPM forecasts $450B AI supply in 2027; hyperscaler FCF negative through 2028 with $595B funding gap
bullets.body: JPMorgan's TMT credit team forecasts $450B of AI-related supply in 2027 ($225B parent issuance + $225B GPU/data center financing), with aggregate hyperscaler FCF negative through 2028 and a ~$595B funding gap across 2027–2028. AWS guided ~40% growth; search growth is slowing within the group; Meta has the clearest near-term AI returns through advertising.

bullets.title: Growth-to-value rotation intensifies: Russell 1000 Growth underperforms Value by ~30 ppts YTD
bullets.body: Russell 1000 Growth is underperforming Russell 1000 Value by approximately 30 percentage points year-to-date, with S&P 500 up only ~7% but showing record dispersion between sectors. Quality/high-beta ratio has climbed from 0.15 to 0.34 as real 2-year yields rose 73bps over 13 weeks. Nominal demand-sensitive sectors (Energy, Industrials, Materials) are under pressure while early cyclicals and secular growers outperform.

bullets.title: 52-week lows dominated by Tech/China: IREN -69%, NFLX -48%, BABA -46% from highs
bullets.body: 37 large-cap stocks (>$5B market cap) hit 52-week lows on 11/19, with the worst drawdowns in IREN (-68.8%), NFLX (-47.8%), and BABA (-45.5%) from their 52-week highs. Largest new high clusters are in Finance, Technology Services, and Communications — consistent with the sector rotation theme.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz crude exports at 70% of normal; oil inventories built +13.2 mmbbls last week
bullets.body: Crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz have fallen to ~12.2 mmbbl/d, roughly 70% of the pre-war 18 mmbbl/d norm, with tanker exits at 8/day vs. 35/day normal. US oil inventories built +13.2 mmbbls last week (crude +3.6, refined products +9.7), creating near-term downward price pressure even as supply disruption risk remains. WTI crude was +1.18% in pre-market.

bullets.title: Consumer spending bifurcating: WMT 'stable, resilient'; BBWI cuts 4Q guide, Pottery Barn decelerates
bullets.body: Walmart described the consumer as 'stable, resilient' with US e-commerce +23% and Sam's Club comps +4.9%, raising FY26 EPS guide to $2.84–$2.89. In contrast, BBWI guided 4Q sales -5.5% to -2% (vs consensus -2%) blaming inflation and competition, and WSM's Pottery Barn comped only +1.8% (vs +5.1% prior quarter) — the brand's first meaningful miss in over two years. The divergence between value-oriented and discretionary/aspirational spending is widening.

bullets.title: Taiwan stocks -4.4% overnight; China at cycle lows despite Trump/Xi meeting
bullets.body: Taiwan's EWT fell 4.4% overnight, consistent with the semiconductor export control tightening and broader tech risk-off. Chinese equities remain at cycle lows despite recent diplomatic engagement at the Trump/Xi summit, reflecting the fundamental headwind from US chip restriction escalation.

bullets.title: IEA warns data centers will drive 70% more carbon emissions by 2030; 30/31 moratoriums passed
bullets.body: The IEA projects data-center carbon emissions rising 70% by 2030 as the US and China turn to fossil fuels to power AI workloads. Policy risk is crystallizing: 30 of 31 data-center moratoriums on election ballots passed, while COP31's revised deal omits any reference to fossil fuels and pivots to carbon capture — a potential regulatory overhang for US-based data-center operators.

bullets.title: US Treasury 10-year at 5.097%, regaining flight-to-quality bid as tech sells off
bullets.body: 10-year yields are at 5.097% (+3.1bps), 2-year at 4.839% (+3.9bps), with Treasuries reasserting flight-to-quality characteristics — rallying when tech weakens. Stress remains equity-side only; credit and rates volatility are still relatively calm, suggesting this is a positioning/valuation reset rather than a systemic credit event.
